_comment: Bundled vocabulary for the iac-scan validator (contract requirement 3).
Kept in sync with contract/iac-scan.schema.json by scripts/check_repo.py.
These are the SHAPES a security finding can take — the technologies this piece can read, and
the severity/status/category values Noru's own API publishes for a security finding. They are
not framework content: no control text, no guidance, no evidence-item list. What is already
open, which assets exist and which risks exist all come from the customer's organization at
scan time, never from this file. See contract/README.md, requirement 9.
severity, status and category are the published enums for a Noru security finding. Their source
is the 'Security Findings' entry in the Canonical Values Reference of
https://api.noru.tech/llms.txt. Do not extend them here: a value this piece invents is a value
the API rejects at push time, which is the worst moment to find out.
_status_horizon_days_comment: How long an interpretation of a finding may stand, counted in days from the day the
configuration was observed. The anchor is observed_on and not decided_at on purpose: a finding
observed in March and signed in August is a claim about March's configuration, however recent
An open or in-progress finding is a live observation that the next scan refreshes, so the
window is short. Accepting a misconfiguration, or calling it a false positive, is a human
decision to leave it in place — it gets a longer window, but never an unbounded one, because
an acceptance nobody revisits is how a known misconfiguration becomes permanent.
